image_description: Two male mallard ducks (drakes) floating on green rippled water. The duck in the foreground left is larger and sharper, displaying characteristic breeding plumage: iridescent green head, white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey body. The duck in the background right is smaller due to perspective, showing similar coloration but less detail. Both exhibit a low-floating posture typical of aquatic birds.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both ducks clearly display the characteristic broad, flat, yellow-green bills of a mallard drake. The shape and color are consistent with the taxonomy.
The eyes on both subjects appear as small, dark points, consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bodies are streamlined and sit low in the water, indicating buoyancy and waterproof plumage. The proportions are stocky and compact.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreground duck perfectly matches the mallard drake description: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey flanks. The background duck shows similar coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ducks are floating on water. Their legs and feet are submerged and completely occluded by the water surface and body angle. It is impossible to verify the presence of webbed feet or leg placement visually.
The wings are folded against the body. While not spread, the visible portion shows the correct contour and feather texture consistent with broad, pointed wings folded at rest.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail region is visible on both ducks. The foreground duck shows the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (drake feathers) typical of mallards.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The water ripples have a slightly repetitive, 'painted' texture rather than natural fluid dynamics. There is minor smudging where the duck bodies meet the water line, lacking sharp displacement or realistic reflection boundaries.

The background duck exhibits excessive softness and lack of feather definition compared to the foreground. While depth-of-field blur is expected, the transition feels artificial, resembling a generative blur rather than optical bokeh.
The white neck ring on the foreground duck bleeds slightly into the green head and chestnut breast. The edges are not crisp, suggesting minor fusion or blending artifacts common in AI generation.
